glosses: to look, glance; (especially) to peek, spy
neugierig und heimlich gucken (spionieren)

examples.text: Die Kinder luscherten durchs Fenster, um ihre Geschenke schon vor dem Weihnachtsabend zu sehen.
Beim Versteckspiel hat Marcus, der Schummler, schon wieder geluschert.
Als Rene sich umgezogen hat, hat Sandra heimlich geluschert.
Hafen-Lyrik: …durchs Fenster luschert man in Kneipen - um so die Zeit sich zu vertreiben…
Da hab ich gewusst, dass sie auch heimlich luschert. »Du schummelst!«, habe ich gesagt.
»Woher weißt du denn, dass ich Badesachen dabei habe?« »Ich hab geluschert.«
Zu gerne wäre ich aufgesprungen und hätte um die Ecke geluschert. Das ging natürlich nicht.

„Für den einen bedeutet "luschern" so viel wie heimlich gucken ("He, du luscherst ja, das ist unfair!"), für den anderen heißt es "schlafen": "Gute Nacht! Luscher schön!". Bei solchen Bedeutungsunterschieden ist ein Wunder, dass sich die Norddeutschen untereinander überhaupt verstehen.“

glosses: friedlich und fest schlafen

translations.source_sense_description: umgangssprachlich, norddeutsch: neugierig und heimlich gucken (spionieren)

glosses: A short, soft, high-pitched sound, as made by a baby bird.
A feeble utterance or complaint.

examples.text: I don't want to hear a peep out of you!

glosses: The sound of a steam engine's whistle; typically shrill.

examples.text: With a "peep" from a high-pitched whistle, the train would leave by the crossover to the down line, […].

"Peep, peep," said Edward, "I'm ready."
"Peep, peep, peep," said Henry, "so am I."

glosses: A sandpiper or other small wader.
To make a soft, shrill noise like a baby bird.
To speak briefly with a quiet voice.
To look, especially through a narrow opening, or while trying not to be seen or noticed.

examples.text: The man peeped through the small hole.

And it was while all were passionately intent upon the pleasing and snake-like progress of their uncle that a young girl in furs, ascending the stairs two at a time, peeped perfunctorily into the nursery as she passed the hallway—and halted amazed.

But Richmond[…]appeared to lose himself in his own reflections. Some pickled crab, which he had not touched, had been removed with a damson pie; and his sister saw, peeping around the massive silver epergne that almost obscured him from her view, that he had eaten no more than a spoonful of that either.

glosses: To begin to appear; to look forth from concealment; to make the first appearance.

examples.text: When flowers first peeped, and trees did blossoms bear.

They first caught crabs and quohogs in the sand; grown bolder, they waded out with nets for mackerel; more experienced, they pushed off in boats and captured cod; and at last, launching a navy of great ships on the sea, explored this watery world; put an incessant belt of circumnavigations round it; peeped in at Behring’s Straits; and in all seasons and all oceans declared everlasting war with the mightiest animated mass that has survived the flood; most monstrous and most mountainous!

glosses: To take a look at; check out.

examples.text: Did you peep that video I sent you?
Peep me, I'm fabulous, I work with the hardest working women at Kay Jeweler's, selling the finest jewels to the richest people.

glosses: To see, uncover.

examples.text: A lot of females were hesitant about getting with Pimp. He had a hard edge to him that made it impossible not to peep his cruel nature.

glosses: A quick look or glimpse, especially a furtive one.

examples.text: I was sick with dread, but I bravely said: "I'll just take a peep inside. / I guess he's cooked, and it's time I looked"; […] then the door I opened wide.
So saying she loosened some ivory screws of the guitar, so as to open a peep lengthwise through its interior.

But at last Mr. Fox gave the order to stop. "I think," he said, "we had better take a peep upstairs now and see where we are. I know where I want to be, but I can't possibly be sure we're anywhere near it."

Another wheel toy was a baker's barrow on wheels, 14 inches high; it was filled with buns, loaves, and crumpets and came from Hamley's. This toy in 1959 was a peep into the past, for wheeled barrows such as this one, had not been in use for a number of years.
He did manage a brief peep at the building’s Rotunda as he called on members of the Senate Judiciary Committee in July.

glosses: The first partial appearance of something; a beginning to appear.

examples.text: the peep of day

glosses: A peepshow.

examples.text: A boring lusterless attempt at pornography, a niche above the racks of pulp pocketbooks sold in the front room of peeps.

glosses: A spot on a die or domino.
A person.

translations.source_sense_description: umgangssprachlich, norddeutsch: neugierig und heimlich gucken (spionieren)

glosses: To look slyly, or with the eyes half closed, or through a crevice; to peep.
To be only slightly, partially visible, as if peering out from a hiding place.

examples.text: A pale strip of white skin peeked out from under his waistband.
Her brown skin peeked through the empty gap in her clothing.

glosses: To retrieve (a value) from a memory address.

examples.text: We are peeking the value from the first index's memory location.

glosses: A quick glance or look.
Misspelling of pique.
